client_dev: Hey team — customer on Go clientlib v0.9 sees intermittent 401s on the streaming SSE endpoint when the client reconnects after a keepalive. Happened ~20x today. request-id: r-0a1b2c3d. I tried a quick curl and it returns 401 unless I include the cookie header. Can someone advise a minimal curl repro and what headers to capture?

support_jen: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl you tried and the request-id from the server logs? Also which auth flow (short-lived bearer vs signed cookie)? :thinking_face:

client_dev: Auth is short-lived Bearer tokens from our auth proxy (60s TTL). Here's the stripped curl I used (token replaced):

```bash
curl -v -N \\\"https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/stream?model=gpt-lite\\\" \\\\ \\--header \\\"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\\\" \\\\--header \\\"Accept: text/event-stream\\\"
```

It yields HTTP/1.1 401 and the body is empty. But if I add `--cookie 'session=eyJ...'` it returns 200 and starts streaming.

micah: Interesting — clientlib might be failing to send the refreshed Authorization on reconnect. Two quick asks: 1) can you capture the exact upstream request headers from the proxy logs for r-0a1b2c3d? 2) try curl with `--no-buffer` and `--raw` to emulate streaming and include `-H 'Connection: keep-alive'` to match client behavior.

client_dev: Got proxy snippet for r-0a1b2c3d: `Authorization: Bearer REDACTED`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, no Cookie header, `Connection: close` on the *second* request (after reconnect). First request had `Connection: keep-alive`.

ops-miguel: That pattern explains it — proxy is enforcing sticky auth via signed cookie for reconnects in our infra; if the reconnect loses the Authorization header we fall back to cookie auth. Let's try to reproduce the reconnect sequence exactly.

support_jen: Proposed minimal curl sequence to reproduce the race (replace token/cookie):

```bash
# 1) start streaming (simulate initial connect)
curl -v -N \\\"https://api.../v1/stream?model=gpt-lite\\\" \\\ \\--header \\\"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\\\" \\\--header \\\"Accept: text/event-stream\\\" \\\--header \\\"Connection: keep-alive\\\" &

# 2) force reconnect after 2s (kill and re-run with missing auth)
sleep 2; curl -v -N \\\"https://api.../v1/stream?model=gpt-lite\\\" \\\--header \\\"Accept: text/event-stream\\\" \\\--header \\\"Connection: keep-alive\\\"
```

support_jen: Run that and attach both `curl -v` outputs and the proxy access log lines for both requests (include x-request-id). Mask tokens before uploading.

client_dev: Ran it — first request 200, second 401. Attached snippets: first log: `r-0a1b2c3d 200 Connection: keep-alive`, second: `r-0a1b2c3d-1 401 Connection: keep-alive`. Both requests show same x-forwarded-for.

micah: OK — next step: does the clientlib attempt to reattach the original Authorization header on reconnect (race window when token rotated)? If the token rotated between requests, it would cause 401. Can you check token issuance times in auth-proxy logs for that session id?

client_dev: Auth proxy shows token issued at T and rotated at T+45s. The reconnect happened at T+46s. So the client retried with the old token.

ops-miguel: That nails it. Short-term mitigations: 1) ensure clientlib always attaches the latest token on reconnect, 2) add server-side tolerant window (5s) or fallback to signed cookie for reconnects, 3) for support repro: include `--header 'Authorization: Bearer <old_token>'` in second curl to reproduce 401 vs `--cookie` to reproduce success.

support_jen: For the debug bundle: please collect both curl -v captures, the proxy logs for the two request-ids, the auth-proxy issuance/rotation log lines, and the clientlib debug trace (enable CLIENTLIB_LOG=debug for 1 minute). Zip and upload to the secure share. Add the exact commands you executed.

client_dev: Will do. One quick ask — is there a recommended curl flag to better mimic Go net/http behavior for streaming reconnects?

micah: Use `--no-buffer` `--raw` `-H 'Connection: keep-alive'` and run in background then re-run. Also `--http2` if your clientlib negotiates h2. That tends to reproduce the multiplexing edge cases.

engbot: Dev checklist: https://internal.redwood/docs/support/debugging-streaming (contains minimal curl templates, header checklist, and redaction reminder). :white_check_mark:

client_dev: Thanks all — I'll gather the bundle and open a dedicated ticket with the artifacts. Leaving the curl snippets here for future. :pray:
